title: Paper call: Eicher Motors Q3 FY27 consolidated operating margin is ≥24.0%
body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.42 (naive base rate 0.60) that: Eicher Motors Q3 FY27 consolidated operating margin is ≥24.0%. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (13-Nov-2026): record revenue ₹7,422 cr (+20%), EBITDA ₹1,760 cr; Royal Enfield Q2 volume 376,722 (+15%), YTD Apr–Oct ~+18%, bookings +21% YTD, 'highest-ever monthly sales in September and October', channel stock below normal. Three price hikes in CY26; CEO Vidhya Srinivasan: 'we don't give forward-looking guidances… there is volatility'; MD Govindarajan: 'the range bound on the percentage is not what is driving us… absolute profit'; analyst notes 'other expenditure surge'. Screener OPM (OP÷Sales): Q3 FY26 25.5% (1,557/6,114), Q4 FY26 24.9%, Q1 FY27 24.0% (1,591/6,632), Q2 FY27 23.7% (1,760/7,422). Cheyyar module 1 started Q2 FY27 (capacity 1.65 mn), module 2 pulled into Q4 FY27. Reasoning: Management repeatedly steered analysts away from margin percentage toward absolute profit while costs (steel, freight, marketing, new-plant ramp) rise — a tone we read as a soft warning. Two consecutive quarters at/below 24% and new capacity costs lean below the naive 'stays near recent levels' base. Resolution: YES if Eicher Motors' consolidated Operating Profit ÷ Sales for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026, from screener.in's consolidated quarterly table (or recomputed as EBITDA ÷ revenue from operations from the results filing), is ≥24.0% (one decimal). Source: Eicher Motors Q3 FY27 results (NSE filing) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table. Resolve by 2027-02-28; score with Brier vs base rate.

title: Paper call: ICICI Bank reports a higher net interest margin for Q4 FY27 than for Q3 FY27
body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.62 (naive base rate 0.45) that: ICICI Bank reports a higher net interest margin for Q4 FY27 than for Q3 FY27. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Oct-2026): NIM 4.18% vs 4.36% in Q1 (4.28% ex tax-refund interest); drag from ~$18 bn FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI swap window and lower CASA (9–10 bp mix impact). CFO Sandeep Batra: 'The full impact would largely get reflected in the third quarter, after which we expect the margins to start moving up, even based on the current level of policy rates'; 'when repo repricing happens, there is a positive movement on the NIM… repo rates can go up to 6%… another two hikes'. Loans +30% YoY (24% ex FCNR-funded), deposits +27%, provisions ₹851 cr (0.2% of advances). Reasoning: This is a dated, specific promise (margins trough in Q3, rise thereafter) from a bank whose margin guidance has generally been reliable, and the rate-hike cycle reprices ICICI's large repo-linked book faster than deposits. Risks: deposit repricing and FCNR deployment. Above base. Resolution: YES if the net interest margin ICICI Bank reports for Q4 FY27 (Jan–Mar 2027) in its Q4 results/presentation is strictly greater than the NIM it reports for Q3 FY27 (as stated in the Q3 release, both on the bank's headline basis). Equal = NO. Source: ICICI Bank Q3 and Q4 FY27 results press releases / investor presentations (NSE). Resolve by 2027-05-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

Management: 'long-term ARPU growth ultimately depends on a more rational pricing structure where the industry is able to monetize the continued growth in data consumption'; the Q2 'intervention… on prepaid ladder' (discontinuing the ₹299 pack) was 'experimentation on our own base'; 'the architecture correction is a much broader correction that is required in the industry… to move more decisively'. Reasoning: Cycle: Indian telecom takes a headline hike every ~2–2.5 years (Dec-2019, Nov-2021, Jul-2024 — from memory, unverified); by mid-2027 the gap would be ~3 years and capex for 5G/data centres keeps pressure on. But Airtel is talking about 'architecture' (data monetisation) rather than a flat hike, and the leader's timing is unknowable. Slightly above base. Resolution: YES if, between 21-Nov-2026 and 30-Jun-2027, Bharti Airtel announces (press release, NSE filing or widely reported company statement) increases to its prepaid mobile tariffs under which its most popular 28-day unlimited plan price rises ≥10%. Plan withdrawals, validity cuts or postpaid-only changes = NO. Source: Bharti Airtel press releases / NSE announcements; national press coverage. Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

title: Paper call: Titan's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats the Nifty 50's price return
body: Forward test of the valuation-temperature method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.45 (naive base rate 0.48) that: Titan's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats the Nifty 50's price return. Evidence: Yahoo close 20-Nov-2026: Titan ₹4,620.0 (52-wk ₹3,751–5,187); Nifty 50 25,800.6. Screener: P/E 57.7 on TTM EPS ₹79.22 (consolidated) vs FY-end P/E (May price ÷ FY EPS) of ~79×, 83×, 86×, 98×, 77× for FY22–FY26 → ~0.7× its own 5-yr median ('cooler than usual'). But TTM earnings are flattered: Q2 FY27 standalone OPM 15% vs 10–11% history included a ~₹490 cr customs-duty gain in jewellery (normalised Titan Jewellery margin 11.1–11.7% per the 11-Nov-2026 call) and gold MTM swings; Q2 standalone sales growth slowed to +8%; coins/investment buying soft. Reasoning: Valuation-temperature test with a twist: the stock looks cool on reported TTM earnings, but on normalised margins the multiple is close to its usual level. If the method only works on clean earnings, it should not help here; we lean slightly under base. Resolution: YES if (Titan NSE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 4,620.0) > (Nifty 50 close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits/bonuses; dividends ignored. Source: NSE / Yahoo Finance closes (TITAN.NS, ^NSEI). Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

title: Paper call: Polycab India Q3 FY27 consolidated operating margin is ≥13.0%
body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.72 (naive base rate 0.70) that: Polycab India Q3 FY27 consolidated operating margin is ≥13.0%. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Oct-2026): revenue record (+53% YoY per screener: ₹9,899 cr), EBITDA margin 14.4% (+50 bps QoQ); W&C EBIT margin 14.2%; FMEG EBIT 10.1% (first double-digit), FMEG growth +124% (solar). Management keeps the W&C medium-term EBITDA guide at '11% to 13%' and flags 'near-term inflationary pressures… surfacing'. Screener OPM: Sep-24 11.5%, Dec-24 13.8%, Mar-25 14.7%, Jun-25 14.5%, Sep-25 15.8%, Dec-25 12.7%, Mar-26 13.1%, Jun-26 13.8%, Sep-26 14.4%. Reasoning: Management talks conservatively (11–13% guide) while delivering above it for most quarters — the mirror image of a hype gap. We side with delivery, shaded for copper/inflation and the Q3 FY26 dip to 12.7%. Resolution: YES if Polycab's consolidated Operating Profit ÷ Sales for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (screener.in quarterly table, or EBITDA ÷ revenue from operations from the results) is ≥13.0%.
